temnitis: temnō, -ere, tempsī, temptum — to scorn, despise, slight (2nd pl. pres.)
tendentemque: tendō, -ere, tetendī, tentum — to stretch out, extend, hold forth (pres. part., m. acc. sg.) + -que 'and'
tendere: tendō, -ere, tetendī, tentum — to stretch, direct one's course, make for (pres. inf.)
tenebat: teneō, -ēre, tenuī, tentum — to hold, keep, grasp (3rd sg. impf.)
testudine: testūdō, -inis (f.) — tortoise; vaulted roof, arch (abl. sg.)
teucrum: Teucrī, -ōrum (m. pl.) — Teucrians, Trojans (gen. pl., archaic -um for -ōrum)
trahebat: trahō, -ere, traxī, tractum — to drag, draw; sorte trahebat, drew by lot (3rd sg. impf.)
trahuntur: trahō, -ere, traxī, tractum — to drag, draw along (3rd pl. pres. pass.)
tristes: tristis, -e — sad, sorrowful, gloomy (f./m. nom. pl.)
troiana: Trōiānus, -a, -um — Trojan, of Troy (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
troianoque: Trōiānus, -a, -um — Trojan, of Troy (m./n. abl. sg.) + -que 'and'
troilus: Troilus, -ī (m.) — Troilus, youngest son of Priam, killed by Achilles (nom. sg.)
tunsae: tundō, -ere, tutudī, tunsum — to beat, pound, strike (perf. pass. part., f. nom. pl.)
turbat: turbō, -āre — to disturb, confuse, trouble (3rd sg. pres.)
turbo: turbō, -inis (m.) — whirlwind, storm, spinning blast (nom. sg.)
tydides: Tȳdīdēs, -ae (m.) — son of Tydeus, Diomedes (nom. sg., Greek patronymic)
urbes: urbs, urbis (f.) — city (nom. pl.; also acc. pl.)
vastabat: vastō, -āre — to lay waste, ravage, devastate (3rd sg. impf.)
vecti: vehō, -ere, vexī, vectum — to carry; pass. to be borne, sail (perf. pass. part., m. nom. pl.)
velis: vēlum, -ī (n.) — sail; canvas, cloth, awning (abl./dat. pl.)
veniam: venia, -ae (f.) — favour, grace, pardon, leave (acc. sg.)
veniant: veniō, -īre, vēnī, ventum — to come (3rd pl. pres. subj.)
venimus: veniō, -īre, vēnī, ventum — to come (1st pl. perf., vēnimus; pres. venīmus)
vero: vērō (adv.) — in truth, indeed, but; tum vērō, then indeed
versa: vertō, -ere, vertī, versum — to turn, reverse (perf. pass. part., f. abl. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
vertere: vertō, -ere, vertī, versum — to turn, change, drive (pres. inf.)
vescitur: vescor, vescī — to feed on, enjoy, live on (+ abl.) (3rd sg. pres. dep.)
vestris: vester, vestra, vestrum — your (pl.) (m./f./n. abl./dat. pl.)
vetant: vetō, -āre, vetuī, vetitum — to forbid, prohibit (3rd pl. pres.)
videbat: videō, -ēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see, behold (3rd sg. impf.)
viri: vir, virī (m.) — man, hero, husband (nom. pl.; gen. sg.)
vis: vīs, vīs (f.) — force, power, violence; pl. vīrēs, strength (nom. sg.)
xanthumque: Xanthus, -ī (m.) — Xanthus, river of Troy (acc. sg.) + -que 'and'
